status.numerical_agreement_basis: Final, 2026-11-05; all 30 in-scope targets produced and comparable. Tolerance kept as recorded: +/-1.0 WER point, from the paper's own statement about its Phoenix2014 re-runs ('We achieved similar results with around 1% fluctuations in WERs', arXiv v1 Sec. V). Assessed on sclite's exact test WER against arXiv v1 Table I; each ArabSign Signer-Indep target is the plain arithmetic mean of its six leave-one-signer-out folds, the aggregation of the paper's Table II Avg column. Within +/-1.0 (7 of 30): SMKD Phoenix SD (-0.17), CorrNet Phoenix SI (+0.80), VAC (+0.1051), SMKD (+0.0351) and TLP (+0.8726) on ArabSign Signer-Dep, and VAC (-0.81) and SMKD (+0.05) on ArabSign Signer-Indep. The other 23 are outside, from -25.80 (VAC GrSL SI) to +87.61 (CorrNet GrSL SI), so the produced set does not agree. Two qualifications, recorded without interpretation: (1) ArabSign Signer-Dep published values are all below 1% WER, so a 1-point absolute tolerance cannot distinguish them; the three 'within' values differ by +37.7%, +16.8% and +357.8% relative. (2) For ArabSign Signer-Indep, none of the 30 per-signer folds is within +/-1.0 of its Table II value: VAC folds differ by -4.15 to +10.10 and SMKD folds by -3.20 to +4.02, so the two 'within' means come from fold differences of both signs (target result.per_fold). Every target result also records the relative difference (reproduced minus published, over published). This is a mechanical comparison; the scientific interpretation is for a human reviewer.
status.preference_level_basis: Level 2, confirmed by this paper's own build, preflights and 55 full runs: all five systems run their pinned official code through its own main.py, with two kinds of correctness patch and dependency/environment fixes only. (1) patches/ctcdecode-cxx17.patch: ctcdecode does not compile against current PyTorch (image build im-zwwdoz4GF7RwJO4BnSPdG6). (2) patches/<repo>-ctc-without-cudnn.patch for VAC_CSLR, TLP, SEN and CorrNet: on PyTorch 2.11/cuDNN 9.19, nn.CTCLoss uses cuDNN for unequal-length batches and returns wrong gradients (cosine 0.06-0.96 vs a float64 reference; runs ctc-diagnostics-*-001, preflight-*-002/003); disabling cuDNN for the CTC call restores the native computation PyTorch 1.x used. Dependencies: lmdb (imported by TLP/SEN), simple-video-utils 0.7.4 with av 18.1.0. New datasets and Phoenix SI5 enter only as data files and dataset configs written with the repos' own preprocess helpers; no upstream code is changed for them.

Signer-Dep test therefore has 1,841 of 1,843 clips and the leave-one-signer-out folds for signers 01, 02 and 05 lose 3, 1 and 1 clips (0.05% of the data overall).

35 file stems carry a signer/sentence prefix that differs from their folder (e.g. 02/test/0007/03_01_0007_(16_02_21_21_01_01)_c.mp4); the folder path, which the author's CSVs list, defines signer, split and sentence, and sample IDs are <signer>_<sentence>_<timestamp> from the path.

The labels give 93 distinct glosses, two fewer than the 95 the ArabSign paper (FG 2023, Sec. III-B and Table II) states; the 155 sign tokens and 3.1 signs per sentence match exactly (vocabulary_check).

vocabulary_check.comparison: The labels used reproduce the paper's 155 signs over 50 sentences and 3.1 signs per sentence exactly; they give 93 distinct glosses against the paper's 95 (procCaption gives 90, further from it). The two-gloss difference is not explained by either label column; it is supporting evidence for the 'Sign Language Sentence' labels, not proof that they are what the paper's authors used. Every split of every setting covers all 93 glosses and 50 sentences (modal_app.py::arabsign_split_record, app ap-4HwGUsgGtScHCYmacWBOAP).

metric_definitions.name: Word error rate (gloss level)
metric_definitions.implementation: Each pinned upstream repo's evaluation: NIST SCTK sclite over CTM hypotheses vs STM references (evaluation/slr_eval), as selected by evaluate_tool: sclite in configs/baseline.yaml
metric_definitions.version: NIST SCTK sclite at commit 9688a26882a688132a5e414cadcb4c19b6fffaba (built in the Dockerfile and symlinked to each repo's ./software/sclite), invoked by each repo's evaluation/slr_eval/wer_calculation.py; the reported value is (S+D+I)/N from sclite's Sum row in the .raw report, which upstream logs to one decimal
metric_definitions.aggregation: corpus-level (S+D+I)/N over the split (paper Eq. 1); ArabSign Signer-Indep = arithmetic mean of 6 per-fold WERs (Table II)

runs.purpose: No training (operator request of 2026-11-05, item 1): extend the adapter-check-002 cross-check to Phoenix SD, Phoenix SI and the six ArabSign LOSO folds. For each setting, modal_app.py::adapter_check copies each of the five full runs' own code directory, compares info lists, gloss dictionaries and ground-truth STMs, and runs each repo's own BaseFeeder on the same 20 clips (10 train, 10 test): label ids and glosses, frames read, frame shape, test-transform tensor and seed-0 train-transform tensor. Only change since adapter-check-002: phoenix-sd, which has no harness dataset name, reads each repo's own phoenix2014 lists as its run did.

terminal.detail: No difference found in any compared item, in any of the eight settings, across the five runs (four repos) of each: every info-list row (fileid, folder, signer, label, num_frames) of train/dev/test, gloss dictionaries (size and every entry), ground-truth STMs, and for the same 20 clips (10 train, 10 test) label ids and glosses, frames read (equal to the list count), frame shape 256x256x3, the test-transform tensor and the seed-0 train-transform tensor (bit-identical sha256). Phoenix SD: VAC/TLP's dataset_preprocess.py lists and SEN/CorrNet's committed lists are identical row for row; train/dev/test 5671/540/629, gloss dict 1,295. Phoenix SI5: 4375/111/180, gloss dict 1,135. LOSO folds 01-06: train 7798/7733/7690/7780/7831/7818, token dev 50, test 1532/1597/1640/1550/1499/1512, gloss dict 93. Decoded labels equal the list label token for token (three Phoenix sample labels contain a double space). Reference tokens unseen in training: Phoenix SD dev 38 of 5,540 and test 45 of 6,504; Phoenix SI5 dev 10 of 1,167 and test 12 of 1,901; none in any LOSO fold. Only the feeder_args key sets differ, as in adapter-check-002.

evidence: arXiv v1 Sec. IV 'Experiments Setup': 'We followed the same experimental settings described in each study' AND 'Adam ... 40 epochs ... batch size of 2 and an initial learning rate of 10^-3, reduced at epochs 20 and 35 by a factor of five'

ICCVW 2025 PDF (sha256 922a2038...) Sec. 3.3: 'The VAC, SMKD, and CorrNet models were trained for 40 epochs ... The models TLP, SEN, and SlowFastSign were trained for 80 epochs, following the training protocols outlined by their respective authors' and, for TLP/SEN/SlowFastSign, 'the learning rate was adjusted at epochs 30 and 60'; lr 1e-3 and batch 2 for all.

Shared Table I cells, arXiv v1 vs ICCVW Table 1 (checked 2026-11-02 from both PDFs): all six TLP values and five of six SEN values are identical at one decimal; SEN GrSL Signer-Indep is 8.09 in v1, 8.0 in ICCVW Table 1 and 8.1 in ICCVW Fig. 3. Across all 30 shared cells, 26 are identical at one decimal, 3 match only by truncation (SMKD Phoenix SI 43.08->43.0, SEN GrSL SI 8.09->8.0, CorrNet ArabSign SI 7.65->7.6), and 1 differs (SMKD Phoenix SD 22.31->22.1). So the TLP/SEN numbers did not change although the stated schedule changed from 40 to 80 epochs; the evidence does not show which schedule produced them.

Per run: epochs x (train frames x train rate + dev frames x eval rate + 5 s checkpoint) + final dev/test scoring + 15 min staging/start-up. gates.reason: Every upstream recipe evaluates a dev split each epoch and (TLP/SEN/CorrNet; VAC/SMKD via per-epoch checkpoints) keeps the dev-best model, but the ArabSign Signer-Dep validation subset is unpublished. The choice decides which clips are trained on and which checkpoint is scored for 5 targets.
evidence: ICCVW 2025 Sec. 3.2: 'The official Signer-Dep split consists of 6,783 training samples, 709 validation samples, and 1,843 testing samples.'
arXiv v1 Sec. IV (the assigned version) describes ArabSign without any validation subset.

The dataset author's per-signer split CSVs (ArabSign-EncoderDec.zip, sha256 6980aec2...) publish only train (7,492 rows) and test (1,843 rows) lists; 7,492 = 6,783 + 709. No list of the 709 clips was found on the ArabSign site, its GitHub repository, the paper pages or the ICCVW page.

The author's own code in that zip (EncoderDec/generator.py, CustomCSVDataset) draws validation with sklearn train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=sentence ID) from the training CSV; on 7,492 rows that is 1,499 clips, not 709, so it does not reproduce the stated split.
Five training-list videos are absent from the RGB release, so 7,489 training rows are usable; the test list has 1,841 of 1,843 videos.

Measured cost (compute-full-table measured_estimate): 5 Signer-Dep runs at 40 epochs about USD 129 with a 709-clip dev list or a token dev list, USD 161 with the 1,841-clip test list evaluated every epoch.

alternatives.description: Hold out exactly 709 of the usable training rows, stratified by sentence ID with random_state 42 (the dataset author's seed and stratification), train on the other 6,780 and select the dev-best epoch as in every other setting.
alternatives.paper_evidence: ICCVW split sizes; author's generator.py convention; upstream dev-best rule.
alternatives.decision_needed: Accept a guessed but size-matched, sentence-stratified validation subset.

alternatives.description: Hold out a uniformly random 709 of the usable training rows (seed 0), otherwise as above.
Train on all 7,489 usable training rows and score the final (40th) epoch; no checkpoint selection. A token dev list only keeps upstream's per-epoch loop running and is not used for selection.
alternatives.paper_evidence: v1 mentions no validation subset; deviates from the ICCVW 6,783/709 partition (about 10% more training data).
alternatives.decision_needed: Accept training on the full training list without selection.

alternatives.description: Use the 1,841-clip test list as upstream's dev split and report the best epoch on it.
alternatives.paper_evidence: Not excluded by either paper text; selects on the test set, so the reported WER is optimistically biased. Not recommended.

resolution.decision: stratified-709-seed42: hold out 709 of the 7,489 usable Signer-Dep training rows, stratified by sentence ID with random_state 42; train on the other 6,780 and select the dev-best epoch (lowest dev WER, earliest on ties) as in every other setting.
resolution.basis: Operator decision at this gate on 2026-11-02 after reviewing the alternatives: size from ICCVW Sec. 3.2 (6,783/709/1,843), seed and stratification from the dataset author's EncoderDec/generator.py convention.
selection_procedure: Rows: the dataset author's <signer>_train.csv rows of ArabSign-EncoderDec.zip (sha256 6980aec2...) that have a video in the RGB release (7,489 of 7,492), in sorted archive-path order (<signer>/train/<sentence>/<stem>.mp4).
Stratum per row: the CSV's sentId (50 sentences).

sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split(rows, test_size=709, random_state=42, stratify=sentence IDs) with scikit-learn 1.8.0 (the container image's version); the 709-row part is the dev list, the rest the train list, both kept in sorted order for train and in the returned order for dev.

Implemented in papers/alyami-2024-cslr-comparative/modal_app.py::_arabsign_lists (dev_rule 'stratified-709-seed42'); the result depends on the input order and the scikit-learn version, both fixed above.

split_record.fileid_list_sha256_definition: sha256 of the split's fileids joined by newlines, in list order

gates.reason: The 30 leave-one-signer-out runs (6 folds x 5 models) have no published dev set, yet upstream evaluates dev every epoch and selects the dev-best model. A checkpoint rule (and what upstream's dev loader reads) must be fixed for 5 targets averaged over 6 folds.
evidence: arXiv v1 Sec. V: 'since the ArabSign dataset does not have a specific set for Signer-Indep evaluation, we follow the same setup used in [8], where we leave out one signer for testing in each trial. This is repeated six times ... We also report the average WER amongst all signers.'

arXiv v1 Sec. V on CorrNet's Signer-Indep result: 'Better results are likely to be obtained by fine-tuning the training parameters using a smaller learning rate and adopting early stopping' — which suggests no dev-based early stopping or selection was used for these folds.
ICCVW 2025 Sec. 3.2 describes the same leave-one-signer-out protocol without a validation set.
Upstream main.py: TLP/SEN/CorrNet save '_best_model.pt' on dev WER each epoch; VAC saves every save_interval epochs and has no best-model rule; the phoenix loader path always builds a dev loader.

Measured cost (compute-full-table measured_estimate): 30 LOSO runs at 40 epochs about USD 803 (final-epoch, token dev list), USD 804 (held-out validation subset), USD 965 (held-out signer evaluated every epoch).

alternatives.description: Train 40 epochs on every clip of the five training signers and score the final-epoch checkpoint on the held-out signer. Upstream's per-epoch dev loop reads a small fixed list (not used for selection), so per-epoch evaluation cost is minimal.
alternatives.paper_evidence: v1's 'adopting early stopping' remark; fixed 40-epoch schedule with LR steps at 20/35.
alternatives.decision_needed: Accept final-epoch scoring for the LOSO folds.

alternatives.description: Carve a validation subset (same rule as chosen for Signer-Dep, about 9.5%) from the five training signers and select the dev-best epoch, as in every other setting.
alternatives.paper_evidence: Consistent with the upstream dev-best rule; not described in either paper; trains on about 9.5% fewer clips.
alternatives.decision_needed: Accept an invented validation subset per fold.

alternatives.description: Use the held-out signer's clips as upstream's dev split and report the best epoch on them.
alternatives.paper_evidence: Not excluded by the papers; selects on the test signer, so WERs are optimistically biased. Not recommended.

resolution.decision: final-epoch: each fold trains 40 epochs (steps 20/35) on every usable clip of the five training signers and scores the final-epoch (epoch 39) checkpoint on the held-out signer; no dev-based selection.
resolution.basis: Operator decision at this gate on 2026-11-02. arXiv v1 Sec. V, on CorrNet's Signer-Indep ArabSign result: 'Better results are likely to be obtained by fine-tuning the training parameters using a smaller learning rate and adopting early stopping', which indicates that no early stopping or dev-based selection was used for the leave-one-signer-out folds.
selection_procedure: Train list: every usable row of the five training signers (author train and test CSVs together), in sorted archive-path order; test list: every usable row of the held-out signer.

Upstream main.py always evaluates a dev split each epoch, so the dev list is a fixed token list that is never used for selection: the first training row of each of the 50 sentences in sorted order (these clips are also trained on; no held-out-signer clip is seen before the final scoring).
evaluate() scores the newest checkpoint and refuses to run unless it is the final epoch (num_epoch - 1).
